description: SPANNING THEME = COLLAPSE OVER A CROSS-UNIT CODEBOOK, one level up from trope_theme's per-arc theme collapse. Where trope_theme decodes the theme of ONE character's arc WITHIN a StoryUnit, this codebook decodes a theme that spans SIBLING StoryUnits -- a relation between two child episodes that is invisible in either episode alone. The composer (domains/nested_reading.compose_spanning_theme) turns the cross-unit structure into a SINGLE-TOKEN skeleton by a mechanical graph read over the children's own minted UnitAction nodes (does an earlier child carry an action agent=A patient=B while a later child carries the REVERSED action agent=B patient=A? -- the actor/recipient role-reversal that IS reciprocity, 'a kindness is repaid'), and that ONE token is decoded against this codebook exactly the way story_tree.decode_seam decodes a seam token against ShapeSignatureStoryBoundary and narrative_structure.decode_slot decodes a slot token against ShapeSignatureNarrative. The THEME VERDICT is always the winning ShapeSignatureSpanningTheme's own `theme` attr, never a Python if/else naming the theme. A cross-unit token no schema covers (SPAN_NONE) mints NOTHING -- the discriminative null (a flat union of two unrelated child themes is NOT a spanning theme).

microtheory.name: spanning_theme
microtheory.description: A theme that spans sibling StoryUnits (the reciprocity of 'The Lion and the Mouse': episode 2's rescue reciprocates episode 1's mercy) recognised by ShapeDecode over a dedicated ShapeSignatureSpanningTheme codebook of cross-unit relation tokens -- one level up from trope_theme's per-arc theme, itself one level up from narrative role and coherence collapse.

attrs.name: reciprocity
attrs.line: A kindness is repaid -- the one acted upon returns the deed to the actor. Invisible in either episode alone; it emerges only from the two episodes together: episode 2's rescue reciprocates episode 1's mercy.
attrs.note: The cross-unit token RETURN_ACTION: an earlier sibling StoryUnit carries an action (agent=A, patient=B) and a later sibling carries the REVERSED action (agent=B, patient=A) over the same two entities -- the actor/recipient role-reversal across episodes that IS reciprocity. Read off the children's own minted UnitAction nodes (a mechanical existence check building the token; the THEME is this schema's verdict, not a Python assignment). A flat union of two child arcs never resembles this token to the codebook -- SPAN_NONE.
